instruction: Design a communication system that allows real-time data exchange between ECUs in a vehicle using AUTOSAR CP, ensuring reliable transmission under varying network conditions and with minimal latency.
output: The system shall support real-time communication between electronic control units (ECUs) in a vehicle using the AUTOSAR Classic Platform (CP) communication layer. Transmission shall occur using the CAN FD protocol with a maximum transmission latency of 10 milliseconds under normal network conditions. The system shall implement a retry mechanism for failed transmission requests, with a maximum of three retries before deactivating the transmission and triggering a diagnostic error. All communication shall be routed through defined PDU (Protocol Data Unit) groups, with each group containing only PDUs of the same direction to ensure consistency and reduce processing overhead. The system shall maintain a transmission mode that is activated only when the ECU is in a valid operational state, as defined by the AUTOSAR mode management interface.

instruction: Implement a secure communication channel between ECUs to prevent unauthorized access and data tampering during data exchange, ensuring integrity and confidentiality of transmitted signals.
output: The system shall implement communication protection mechanisms as defined in the AUTOSAR CP R21-11 standard to ensure data integrity and confidentiality during ECU-to-ECU communication. All transmitted signals shall be authenticated using a cryptographic signature derived from a shared key established during initial configuration. The system shall support secure signal group definitions with data encryption using symmetric key algorithms, ensuring that data remains confidential during transmission. Unauthorized access attempts shall trigger a security violation event, which shall be logged and reported to the central diagnostic system. The communication protection mechanism shall not introduce measurable latency exceeding 5 milliseconds under normal operating conditions.

Communication interfaces between clusters shall be defined using standardized PDU definitions and signal mappings, ensuring interoperability across different development teams. instruction: Support the transmission of large data payloads between ECUs, such as sensor images or diagnostic logs, without exceeding CAN FD message size limits or causing network congestion.
output: The system shall support the transmission of large data payloads via the AUTOSAR CP Large Data COM feature, enabling the transfer of data exceeding the standard CAN FD message size limit of 64 bytes. Data payloads shall be segmented into smaller data chunks, with each chunk transmitted sequentially using a dedicated large data PDU. The system shall manage the segmentation and reassembly process at the receiving ECU, ensuring data integrity and correct order of transmission. The system shall monitor network utilization and dynamically adjust transmission frequency to prevent network congestion, with a maximum data transfer rate of 100 kbps under peak load conditions. Transmission shall be performed only when the receiving ECU is in an active operational state to avoid unnecessary network traffic.

instruction: Design a network monitoring system that detects and logs FlexRay bus errors in real-time for automotive ECUs.

instruction: Ensure the FlexRay network can maintain communication during power transitions and wake-up events between ECUs.

instruction: Implement a driver layer that manages the physical transceiver operations, including error handling and wake-up triggers, for consistent and fault-tolerant operation in embedded automotive systems.
output: The system shall implement a FlexRay transceiver driver that manages the physical layer operations of the FlexRay transceiver. The driver shall support at least three operational modes: sleep, active, and error recovery. When a transceiver error is detected, the driver shall initiate an error recovery sequence and log the error status in a persistent error registry. Upon wake-up, the driver shall report the wake-up reason to the higher-layer software, with the wake-up reason being one of: power-up, message timeout, or external signal trigger. The driver shall ensure that all transceiver operations are synchronized with the FlexRay time service to maintain temporal consistency.
